Imperative 'Consider'. The single 'ye' stands both after the imperative and before the vocative; the ASV's own comma ('Consider, ye brutish') places it with the vocative, and the parallel colon writes 'ye fools' the same way, so the verb keeps only its own word (rule 36). Competing reading: 'Consider ye' with the ye as the verb's subject pronoun (rule 17).
Vocative substantival participle takes the supplied 'ye' written before it (rule 36); see the competing reading noted on the imperative.
